missions.title: Capital follows results: eligible pods trade forward with a seed, an algorithm moves capital to what works, and the drawdown ladder cuts what bleeds
missions.idea: The firm is a multi-manager hedge fund with high turnover
missions.demo: uv run python acceptance/capital_machine.py ($0, offline): made-up pods on a synthetic market live forward days; the allocation table moves capital toward the planted edge, a copy is penalised for correlation, a bleeder is halved at 5%, made reduce-only at 7.5% (its buy is refused), closed at 10%; the good pod is never cut; rebuilding from the ledger gives the same allocations.
missions.notes: Plan session cycle 47. Slice a of Next up 1 (also serves 'The allocation algorithm', 'The central risk ladder'). Exists: Pod.current_allocation, Allocation table, allocation_set event + fund_pod (app/registry/pods.py), per-pod positions/cash, max_drawdown in app/metrics/performance.py, the rule engine (app/strategy/rule.py), the gates' eligible verdict (pitch_judged event). Missing: the centre's capital (config), a seed for an eligible pitch, forward execution of a pod's rule through the OMS (prefer the real order path, e.g. a scripted executor per pod, over writing positions directly), the allocation algorithm (pure, app/; weights, per-pod min/max, max move per step; every move an event with its inputs), the drawdown ladder from the pod's high-water mark (thresholds in config), OMS refusals for reduce-only and closed pods (403/409 + logged event), closing = flatten + capital back to the centre. Capital only on forward days: this is the cure for the known hole 'held-out prices are readable'. Demo must show yes and no for each judge (grows/does not grow; cut/not cut). Left for b/c: hiring a replacement PM, real minds in the machine, firm-level drawdown limits, per-position limits, thinking cost in the score if no metered agents in the demo (keep the term, feed it 0 and one nonzero control). Risk tier: money + OMS → red-team + auditor.

missions.title: A real PM researches a strategy, pitches it, and the app's validation gates give a verdict the Human can read
missions.idea: The pitch, then a full report
missions.demo: uv run python acceptance/pitch_gates.py → ($0, offline) the gates first pass their controls (a planted-signal history passes, pure noise fails, the same strategy tried 1 time vs 200 times loses its deflated Sharpe); then the recorded real PM session replays IDENTICAL and prints the pitch: hypothesis, the strategy rule, every research backtest it ran (attempts counted), and the gate table on the held-out window with each number and PASS/FAIL/null
missions.notes: Plan session cycle 44. Slice 1 of 'The pitch and the gates' (Next up #1); serves the book ideas 'The pitch, then a full report', 'A strategy is an isolated function' and 'Validation gates before capital'. Shape decided by the plan (prime rule, refine in NOW.md): (1) a strategy is DATA, not code, in v1: a small versioned rule language (e.g. strategy-v1: signal momentum|mean-reversion|... with lookback, universe, rebalance every k days, top/bottom n, long-only|long-short, gross) evaluated by deterministic code in app/ as a pure function bars-up-to-t -> target weights. No agent code runs anywhere in v1 (agent-written code in a sandboxed subprocess is a later slice: seal work). (2) Research backtests: an endpoint + MCP tool; every call is an event, counted per pod forever (the deflated Sharpe's N cannot be hidden); research may only use bars up to today minus a held-out window. (3) The pitch: an endpoint + MCP tool with hypothesis text, data needed, the strategy rule, team and budget asked; physics runs the gates on the held-out window (still before today: the look-ahead guard holds) and records pitch_submitted + pitch_judged with every number. Gates: IC (mean rank IC and the number of predictions; per regime later), deflated Sharpe (Bailey & Lopez de Prado, N = the pod's attempts), capacity (simple impact vs the bars' volume), correlation with the other pods' return streams (null when there are none: null, not 0), hypothesis recorded but NOT judged by physics (no LLM in app/: the debate / backtest operator judges it, a later slice). Thresholds in config/laws, never hard-coded. v1 grants no capital (allocation is Next up #2): the verdict says 'eligible' or not. (4) Read side for the Human: GET /pitches, GET /pitches/{id} (+ MCP tools), shown in the demo. (5) Positive AND negative controls in the demo: the synthetic market is pure GBM (no signal), so every honest strategy should fail there; a gate that only rejects would pass a reject-only check, so the gate engine is also fed a planted-signal history (generated in the acceptance script, through the same pure functions) that must pass. (6) One real PM (Haiku 5.5 via OpenRouter, specs/pitch-desk/, small key) researches for a few sim-days and pitches; recorded once (cassette), replayed at $0 by the demo. OpenRouter credit ~$1.60 (2026-10-16). Risk tier: new permissions (who may backtest/pitch, pod-scoped) in app/registry/permissions.py + a real spend run -> red-team + auditor before merge. An ADR for the strategy language and the gate law. Left out: agent code in a sandbox, backtest operator, bull/bear debate, capital granted, IC per regime, factor attribution. Merged cycle 46 (3 build sessions): red-team 4 holes (2 fixed, 2 written down), auditor BLOCK (pod-less reader) fixed.

missions.title: Real AI agents (a PM and two analysts) live a backtest month on fake money, each day getting their data package, and we see what they did and what it cost
missions.idea: The backtest: real AI agents in a sealed box, fed a month day by day
missions.demo: uv run python acceptance/real_agents_backtest.py → replays the recorded real-model month in evidence/real-agents-backtest/ at $0 (IDENTICAL), then prints day by day what the PM and the two analysts saw, said and traded, and what each one cost
missions.notes: Plan in state/NOW.md (cycle 42). Host = the app's own runtime (ADR-047). OpenRouter account credit ~$1.86 on 2026-10-16 (the Human's own keys: never touch them): use a cheap pinned model. Monthly accounting across runs reads every firm- key at the provider. World key for the evidence run = sha256('fund-real-agents-backtest/1'). First idea after the rework (ADR-046). Facts: runtime/native.py wakes a mind with the firm's MCP tools; runtime/gate.py METERED_PROVIDERS = {'fake-metered'} only, so a real metered provider (OpenRouter, one key per agent, sum of limits <= the $50/month cap; provisioning key in the gitignored .env as FUND_OPENROUTER_PROVISIONING_KEY) is new money/physics code -> red-team + auditor. Decide the agent host first (book: 'Who hosts the agents'). The acceptance check must cost $0: replay the recorded month (cassette + replay --verify) and check recorded artifacts. missions.title: A metered pod month: every (fake) dollar a mind spends is charged by the system to that mind, and its self-report no longer counts
missions.question: Can the Runtime wake a spending mind only when the system meters it, and can every dollar of a run be attributed to one agent from the meter alone? (Era I EC4; vision M4)
missions.demo: uv run python acceptance/M-001.py → a two-mind pod (PM + Analyst) on the fake metered provider lives a month under an injected numeric cap on a local App; prints, per agent, the provisioner's charges, the App's system-reported cost and the self-report gap (equal / non-zero), the leaderboard costs taken from the meter, the sum of metered $ == the provisioner's total, and that the same specs under the real law (cap null) are refused before physics is told
missions.notes: Raw material: BACKLOG R-6b (ADR-041 §8): gate lets a `metered` provider wake under a numeric cap; provision mints one key per agent (limit ≤ MAX_METERED_USD_MICROS, total ≤ cap); FakeMeteredProvider charges the FakeProvisioner; sync after the last step; fail loudly on a 422 label; expose reader conflicts/malformed (c34 WARN 3); Reuse runtime/metering.py (FakeProvisioner, sync_costs), runtime/gate.py decide_wake_under(provider, adapter, law), app metering endpoint. The real governance cap stays null: a numeric cap exists only as an injected Governance in tests/acceptance; the CLI never accepts an injected law (Art. 4). IDEAS c34: one whole-ledger invariant (sum of authoritative costs == sum of per-key maxima) is the EC4 assertion. RED-TEAM: yes (gate + metering). Parked, not in scope: B-000k (pod-less firm spend), B-000n (cost-report rate), B-022 (secret scan — before any real key). Deferred by the plan (cycle 38): (1) the compare-ledgers law for a metered recording; M-001 refuses `--cassette` on a metered run, so no metered run can be replayed yet. (2) The O(n²) scan in `record_metered_usage` does not matter at one sync per run; it stays in BACKLOG.

missions.title: A run is a self-contained proof object: one cassette file is enough to re-live a month and prove its ledger identical
missions.question: Can anyone re-run a recorded month from the cassette alone (no flags to remember) and get a machine verdict 'identical ledger' or the first divergence? (Era I EC2 path, ticked only with real minds; vision §1 proof objects; prerequisite of the fork instrument)
missions.demo: FUND_MARKETDATA__SYNTHETIC_KEY=<hex> uv run fund-runtime backtest --world specs/desk-month/world.json --specs specs/desk-month --input specs/desk-month/input.json --steps 31 --cassette $TMPDIR/m.cassette.json, then from any directory with the same key: uv run --project <repo> fund-runtime replay --cassette $TMPDIR/m.cassette.json --verify → 'IDENTICAL: <n> events, 0 differences, $0' (and a tampered cassette → 'DIVERGED at step <s>, wake <id>, …'); or uv run python acceptance/M-002.py
missions.notes: Raw material: BACKLOG R-4b-2b: cassette v2 carries run parameters (steps, days_per_step, max_tool_calls, workflow_input), each spec's digest, each wake's model, optional tools_sha256; reader size cap; c32 NOTE 4 (a replay setup error must not read as diverged:…:ended); c32 NOTE 5 (`key` can mislabel a surface change); replay into a fresh DB and run app/ledger/compare.py in one command; a cassette step in scripts/smoke_run.py. v1 cassettes must still be read (or refused by name, decided by ADR). Reuse runtime/cassette.py, runtime/replay.py, runtime/cli.py, app/ledger/compare.py (read-only, one allowed difference — never widen it). Fold B-051 (operator read `fund-env run-minds`, smoke uses it) if it costs < 1/2 session. RED-TEAM: no unless the plan touches the gate or physics; the auditor checks the claim 'one file is enough'. If cassette v2 carries a metered run (M-001), this mission owns the trailing `cost_metered` block law in `app/ledger/compare.py`, by its own ADR (sketch in ADR-044 §6). Otherwise the first mission that replays a metered run (R-8) owns it. Plan (c40): the recording needs its own world (`backtest --world FILE`, a recipe; operator-hosted `--server` cassettes carry no world/ledger and `--verify` refuses them by name); v1 cassettes refused by name (ADR-045); cost_metered stays out of scope (metered `--cassette` still exit 2); B-051 folded into M4, droppable to BACKLOG; physics-adjacent: app/cli.py + app/ledger/compare.py read-only operator tooling, red-team scoped.

missions.title: The desk pod exists as real OpenClaw agents in an isolated firm profile, certified by `fund-runtime openclaw doctor` (100% static checks); an uncertified mind never wakes
missions.question: Can the firm's minds be set up to the 08_OPENCLAW.md standard by code alone — generated, isolated from the Human's agents, deny-by-default — and refused a wake when they are not? (Era I EC7 static half; deliverable 6b; vision M5)
missions.demo: uv run fund-runtime openclaw render --specs specs/desk-month && uv run fund-runtime openclaw doctor → one line per firm- agent, static checks 1–5 PASS, live probes 6–10 SKIPPED (cap null); then a hand-edited workspace file → doctor FAIL (hash drift) and the Runtime refuses to wake that mind
missions.notes: Dropped 2026-10-16 (Builder v3, ADR-046): re-cut into the ideas book, idea "Who hosts the agents: OpenClaw or the app's own runtime" (bible/IDEAS_BOOK.md). Raw material for that idea. Earlier notes: Raw material: BACKLOG R-7 (B-012, B-012a, B-012b, B-023s seal keys, B-000l loopback MCP URL); OCT POC charters → AgentSpec templates (08 §6). Rule zero first: verify every command and file name against the installed version (/opt/homebrew/bin/openclaw), pin it in runtime/openclaw/VERSION_NOTES.md. Rule one: never touch the Human's ~/.openclaw or any non-firm- agent; backup under umask 077 before the first change. The Builder's Bash sandbox can write only the repo and $TMPDIR: the architect must first verify whether the installed OpenClaw can keep a profile's state/config under a directory we choose (env or flag). If yes, the acceptance check renders + applies + doctors inside a temp dir. If no, split by capability: (a) render + every static check that reads only rendered artifacts, run in a temp dir; (b) apply to ~/.openclaw-firm as a step the Human runs once (question in state/QUESTIONS.md). The acceptance check must skip nothing silently: if `openclaw` is absent it FAILS (it is installed here). Gate change 'no conformance → no wake' → RED-TEAM: yes. Live probes stay skipped while the cap is null (Q-0001).

missions.title: A Truman shock: a scenario file crashes a market on day d of a keyed synthetic month, `system` announces it, a pod lives through it, and the same key + scenario replays to the same ledger
missions.question: Can the world script events — the lever by which the Builder changes the world without touching a mind (Art. 10) — deterministically and on the record? (Era I deliverables 4–5: Truman v1 + world events; prerequisite of Era II EC2)
missions.demo: uv run fund-runtime backtest --specs specs/desk-month --steps 31 --scenario scenarios/crash-day-12.yaml → day 12: a `world_event` + `system` announcement in the ledger, the shocked ticker's close drops by the scenario's amount, the scripted pod's equity curve shows it; run twice → compare-ledgers IDENTICAL
serves: Era I deliverable 4 (Truman v1, synthetic half)
missions.notes: Dropped 2026-10-16 (Builder v3, ADR-046): re-cut into the ideas book, idea "Market shocks as world events" (bible/IDEAS_BOOK.md). Raw material for that idea. Earlier notes: Raw material: B-007 (world events table + system announcements), B-008 (Truman v1). Built on the keyed synthetic market (ADR-030), not on a real-history pack: fetching real history needs network the Builder's sandbox does not have (the real-history pack is a later mission or a one-time command the Human runs). The scenario is part of the run's world (ADR-031: run_started.world records it; agents see 'withheld' per ADR-034, the announcement is what they are told). The look-ahead guard holds: no agent learns of a shock before its day. Whether an agent is told its data is synthetic is an experimental variable (08 §4) — record it per run. RED-TEAM: yes (marketdata).

missions.title: Central risk acts by law: a pod driven down by a Truman crash has its capital cut at 5% drawdown, goes reduce-only at 7.5% and is liquidated and closed at 10% — exactly, on the record
missions.question: Can physics enforce the firm's risk ladder (04_FIRM §5) deterministically, so a pod's death is a law, not a judgement? (Era II EC2: 'a forced-drawdown Truman scenario triggers 5% / 7.5% / 10% actions exactly')
missions.demo: uv run python acceptance/M-006.py → a scripted pod lives a month with a 3-step crash scenario; prints the high-water mark, each threshold crossing (day, drawdown %), the ledger event for each action, a refused new-risk order after 7.5% (403/409 + event), and the pod closed with zero positions after 10%
missions.notes: Dropped 2026-10-16 (Builder v3, ADR-046): re-cut into the ideas book, idea "The central risk ladder" (bible/IDEAS_BOOK.md). Raw material for that idea. Earlier notes: Starts Era II while Era I's real-mind criteria wait on the Human's cap (ADR-043). 04_FIRM §5: drawdown from the pod's high-water mark within the generation; 5% → allocation cut to 50%, positions above the new limit reduced within 2 sim-days or by the OMS; 7.5% → reduce-only (+ mandatory review workflow: record the event only, the CRO/CEO workflow is a later mission); 10% → liquidated, closed for the generation. Firm-level 8%/12% and exposure limits: out of scope (next mission). Reuse app/metrics/equity.py and the OMS; every action is an event, derived state rebuildable from the ledger. RED-TEAM: yes (oms).
